questions.question: Who established the Han dynasty?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Han dynasty was established by Liu Bang.
Incorrect. Wang Mang established the Xin dynasty, not the Han dynasty.
Incorrect. Xiang Yu was a hegemon who appointed Liu Bang as prince of Hanzhong, but did not establish the Han dynasty.
Incorrect. Emperor Wu was a later Han emperor who reigned from 141â87 BC, not the founder of the dynasty.

questions.question: Which dynasty preceded the Han dynasty?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Han dynasty was preceded by the short-lived Qin dynasty (221â206 BC).
Incorrect. The Xin dynasty interrupted the Han dynasty between the Western and Eastern Han periods; it did not precede the Han.
Incorrect. The Tang dynasty came much later (618â907 AD) and is mentioned only as the dynasty until which Han coinage remained standard.
Incorrect. The Zhou dynasty (c. 1050â256 BC) is mentioned as when the money economy was first established, not as the dynasty immediately preceding the Han.

questions.question: What year did the Han dynasty come to an end?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Han dynasty came to an end in 220 AD when Cao Pi usurped the throne from Emperor Xian.
Incorrect. 9 AD marks the end of the Western Han and the beginning of the Xin dynasty interruption, not the end of the entire Han dynasty.
Incorrect. 202 BC marks the beginning of the Han dynasty under Liu Bang (Emperor Gaozu).
Incorrect. 280 AD marks the end of the Three Kingdoms period, which succeeded the Han dynasty.

questions.question: What are the two periods into which the Han dynasty is separated?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Han dynasty is separated into two periodsâthe Western Han (202 BC â 9 AD) and the Eastern Han (25â220 AD).
Incorrect. 'Former Han' is another name for the Western Han, and 'Later Han' is not used in the article as a paired period name with it.
Incorrect. Qin and Xin are separate dynasties that preceded and interrupted the Han, respectively.
Incorrect. The article does not divide the Han dynasty into Northern and Southern Han periods.

questions.question: Which philosophy did the Chinese court officially sponsor from the reign of Emperor Wu onward?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that from the reign of Emperor Wu onward, the Chinese court officially sponsored Confucianism in education and court politics.
Incorrect. Taoist religious societies are mentioned later as challenging imperial authority, but they were not officially sponsored from Emperor Wu's reign.
Incorrect. Legalism is not mentioned in the article as being sponsored by the Han court.
Incorrect. Buddhism is not mentioned in the article.

questions.question: In what year did the Han government nationalize private salt and iron industries?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Han government nationalized private salt and iron industries in 117 BC.
Incorrect. 119 BC is when the coinage minted by the central government remained the standard, not when salt and iron were nationalized.
Incorrect. 133 BC is when Emperor Wu began a series of military campaigns against the Xiongnu.
Incorrect. 202 BC is the founding year of the Han dynasty.

questions.question: Which invention is listed among the significant advances in science and technology during the Han period?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article lists the invention of papermaking among the significant advances in science and technology during the Han period.
Incorrect. The printing press is not mentioned in the article.
Incorrect. Gunpowder is not mentioned in the article.
Incorrect. The compass is not mentioned in the article.

questions.question: Which nomadic confederation did the Han dynasty have many conflicts with?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Han dynasty had many conflicts with the Xiongnu, a nomadic confederation centered in the eastern Eurasian steppe.
Incorrect. The Xianbei are mentioned as later overrunning lands north of the Han's borders, not as the group with which the Han had many conflicts.
Incorrect. The Yuezhi are not mentioned in the article.
Incorrect. While both groups are mentioned, the article specifically says the Han had many conflicts with the Xiongnu.

questions.question: Which city was chosen as the new capital of the reunified empire under Han?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Chang'an (modern Xi'an) was chosen as the new capital of the reunified empire under Han.
Incorrect. Luoyang is not mentioned in the article as the Han capital.
Incorrect. Nanjing is not mentioned in the article.
Incorrect. Beijing is not mentioned in the article.

questions.question: Who usurped the throne from Emperor Xian to end the Han dynasty?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Han dynasty came to an end in 220 AD when Cao Pi, king of Wei, usurped the throne from Emperor Xian.
Incorrect. Cao Cao is not mentioned in the article; his son Cao Pi is the one who usurped the throne.
Incorrect. Wang Mang established the Xin dynasty and interrupted the Han, but did not end it by usurping from Emperor Xian.
Incorrect. Liu Bang founded the Han dynasty; he did not end it.
